scope: Read-only diagnosis of native Linux CI compile failure; no source edits, Cargo, cache deletion, dispatch, or rerun.

shared.derive_feature: default -> derive -> dep:rig-derive0.40.0; lib.rs187-189 cfgderive export; registry proc-macro=true

confirmed_defect: Runner changed ubuntu-latest(24.04) to22.04 while preserving cache namespace; native compiled proc-macro target artifacts from newer distribution are restored verbatim and reused. Cache key covers kernel OS class/arch/toolchains/manifests, not distribution ABI.
causal_inference: Strong evidence that cross-distribution native cached artifact is the failing boundary: exact same artifact set passed the old job, only path crates recompile, no rig-derive compilation occurs, and new job fails locating its proc-macro. This is not a missing dependency/feature/source change.
limits: Raw nonverbose E0463 gives no dlopen errno/required GLIBC symbol or artifact pathname; actual cached ELF was not inspected. A particular GLIBC version cannot be asserted as proven. Fresh Ubuntu22-partitioned owning job is required for final confirmation.

minimal_fix.effect: Pinned setup action forwards to rust-cache key; pinned config.ts constructs both primary and restore prefixes with this input before OS/arch/environment. Thus incompatible old cache cannot match, while future Ubuntu22 cache remains reusable. No blanket cache deletion or dependency change.

optional_precise_loader_diagnostic: If retaining old artifact evidence before isolation is useful on an authorized runner: file/ldd -v target/debug/deps/librig_derive-*.so; no library execution or cargo rebuild needed. Not performed here.
